1700000068000.title: Outreach Coordinator
1700000068000.requirements:
NYC Votes non-partisan voter engagement outreach. Civil service title ANALYST CFB AL 2&3 - 0660A.

Minimum qualifications:
1. A bachelor's degree including or supplemented by at least twelve semester credits in accounting, auditing, business or public administration, computer science, economics, finance, statistics, graphic design, personnel or human resources administration, user experience design, or a closely related area of study, AND one year of satisfactory full-time experience in one of those fields; or
2. A four-year high school diploma or equivalent and five years of experience as described in "1"; or
3. Education and/or experience equivalent to "1".

Also listed: ability to move and carry objects up to 20 pounds over 50–100 m between stops; ability to break down complex civics topics for an audience; event planning and program execution including logistics and resource distribution.

1700000068000.notes: Found on Handshake (CUNY SPH board) 8/27/26. BLOCKER TO RESOLVE: the twelve-credit requirement in accounting/business or public admin/CS/economics/finance/statistics/graphic design/HR/UX is not obviously satisfied by a BS in Biology with a Film Studies minor. Applying means going through route 2 or 3 and arguing five years of program and business administration as equivalent — check the transcript for statistics or business credits before writing. Handshake's matcher says 'you do not match any qualifications,' which reflects its major filter, not this requirement text. Cover letter goes in the attachment or 'Message to the Hiring Team' field on SmartRecruiters.

scoreRationale.qualification: The twelve-credit coursework gate is not clearly met by a biology degree, so this depends entirely on the experience or equivalency route being accepted.
scoreRationale.enjoyment: Field-heavy: tabling, carrying materials between stops, live civics presentations, and event logistics — the public-facing end of the spectrum she consistently scores down.
scoreRationale.school: Hybrid, so the in-person load is the lightest of the full-time roles in this batch alongside evening classes.
scoreRationale.location: Bushwick to Lower Manhattan is roughly 40 minutes and only part of the week is onsite.
scoreRationale.mph: Civic participation work is equity-aligned but builds nothing toward public health policy or evaluation.
scoreRationale.mission: Removing barriers to voting and small-donor participation is the structural equity work she targets.

1700000069000.title: FDNY World Trade Center Research Coordinator
1700000069000.org: Montefiore Medical Center — FDNY WTC Health Program
1700000069000.location: New York, NY — hybrid or onsite (WORKSITE UNVERIFIED: Montefiore Bronx vs. FDNY WTC program offices in Brooklyn)
1700000069000.requirements:
Coordinate data linkages between the WTC Health Program and state cancer registries, death registries, and other sources; maintain IRB materials and data use agreements across 15+ studies (protocols, continuing review progress reports, amendments); assist with sub-study recruitment and enrollment, grant submissions, and research team meeting coordination. Monitors the health of 14,000+ firefighters and EMS personnel post-9/11.

Required skills:
- Excellent problem solving, analytical, writing and communication skills
- Experience using Excel and related tools
- Ability to work in a team and independently
- Ability to multitask across several projects
- Master's degree in public health OR bachelor's degree with two or more years of work experience in an academic or public health/research setting
- Experience with grant writing and/or peer reviewed publications
1700000069000.notes: Found on Handshake (CUNY SPH board) 8/27/26. Best full-time role in the Handshake batch. Two soft gaps to address in the cover letter rather than ignore: (1) the experience route specifies an academic or public health/research setting, and her five years are in housing and social services nonprofits; (2) grant writing and/or peer reviewed publications is listed as a required skill — the Grantsmanship Center certificate and grant compliance work cover the grant side, there are no publications. The bachelor's-plus-experience route means the in-progress MPH is not a blocker. VERIFY WORKSITE BEFORE APPLYING — the FDNY WTC Health Program operates out of Brooklyn while Montefiore is Bronx-based, and that is the difference between a 25-minute and a 60-minute commute.

scoreRationale.qualification: Clears the degree-plus-experience route on paper, but the posting asks for a research setting she has not worked in and for publications she does not have.
scoreRationale.enjoyment: Documentation, data use agreements, registry coordination, and meeting logistics with no caseload and no supervisory duty is close to the exact shape of work she wants.
scoreRationale.school: Full-time with an onsite component, so evening classes are workable but not effortless.
scoreRationale.location: Scored conservatively pending worksite confirmation; a Bronx site is roughly an hour from Bushwick, a Brooklyn site would be among the best commutes in the pipeline.
scoreRationale.mph: Occupational and environmental health surveillance of a large cohort, with named opportunities for peer-reviewed publication, is the most directly MPH-building role in this batch.
scoreRationale.mission: Monitoring the long-term health of 9/11 firefighters and EMS responders is unambiguously public-interest work.

1700000073000.title: Community Session Co-Facilitator — LIFHE Project
1700000073000.location: New York, NY — hybrid; sessions in person at CUNY SPH, Harlem
1700000073000.salary: $2,000 stipend for the semester — ~$56–100/hr (20–36 hrs total: 4–6 sessions at 5–6 hrs per session week)
1700000073000.requirements:
Co-facilitate two-hour governance lab sessions with small groups of community members at CUNY SPH in Harlem for Locally Informed Futures for Health Equity (LIFHE), a two-year project developing a community-centered governance framework for health AI, run in partnership with the Harlem Health Initiative at CUNY SPH. Two openings.

Qualifications — applicants should:
- Be an alum or graduate student at CUNY SPH in good academic standing
- Have experience facilitating groups, workshops, or community meetings, and be comfortable facilitating discussion among people with different perspectives
- Be available for sessions at CUNY SPH in Harlem on Wednesday afternoons and early evenings
- Demonstrate clear, plain-language writing skills
- Have an interest in health equity, community engagement or participatory research, and governance of digital health technologies and AI (technical AI background NOT required)
- Have strong organizational skills and comfort managing multiple moving pieces
- Be able to complete CITI human subjects research training before session-based activities

Coursework in community engagement, participatory research, qualitative analysis, or project management is welcome but not required.

Responsibilities: co-facilitate alongside a project team member using a prepared guide; team prep meetings and independent review of facilitation guides; team debriefs plus written debriefs; session logistics, materials, room setup, participant welcome; structured session summaries and handoff of drafted governance language. Project coordination: session scheduling and participant confirmations across three participant groups, timeline and action-item tracking, project management and audit-trail systems, recruitment support with the Harlem Health Initiative and CBO partners.
1700000073000.notes:
Found on Handshake (CUNY SPH board) 8/27/26. TOP-RATED of the Handshake batch — best hours-to-value ratio in the pipeline.

EFFECTIVE HOURLY: $56-100/hr, midpoint ~$73/hr. The 5-6 hrs/week figure applies to weeks that HAVE a session, not every week of the semester — the posting says to expect heavier weeks around sessions and lighter weeks between, and ~5 hrs of intern time per session matches. So 4-6 sessions at 5-6 hrs = 20-36 hrs total for the semester ($100/hr at 20 hrs, $55.56/hr at 36 hrs), averaging about 2 hrs/week across Sept 1-Dec 18. This is 2.5-3.4x the CUNY K-16 rate of $29.32 and the highest effective rate in the pipeline. Worth confirming expected total hours at interview, but the reading is well supported by the posting. Watch for scope creep from the open-ended coordination duties (scheduling across three participant groups, timeline tracking, audit-trail systems, recruitment support) pushing actual hours past the session-based estimate.

SCHEDULE CONFIRMED CLEAR: fall classes meet Tuesday and Thursday late afternoons, in person at CUNY SPH — the same building as the sessions. Wednesday afternoons and early evenings do not conflict. Note one course has weekly assignments due Wednesday nights, so session days double as submission days. Onsite ~3 hrs per session, everything else remote.

APPLY TO info@healthjustice.co with resume and cover letter. The cover letter MUST describe a group, workshop, or meeting she has facilitated and what she learned — her closest evidence is partner office hours, training/TA delivery at United Way, and 15+ community intake events. DO NOT send a writing sample initially; candidates invited to interview provide up to two pages written for a general or community audience, not academic. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis with interviews beginning immediately, so the real deadline is earlier than the 8/31/26 Handshake cutoff in closeDate.

STACKABLE: at roughly 2 hrs/week averaged across the semester this is additive, not a substitute — applicant's own read is that it is reasonable to hold alongside a part-time or even a full-time job. Do NOT treat it as competing with the full-time search; it should run in parallel with whatever lands. This is the only Handshake find in the batch that stacks; Citymeals (20 hrs/wk), Oaklin Lane (25 hrs/wk), NYHF (9-month part-time), and CUNY K-16 (19 hrs/wk) all require a job-sized opening in the schedule.

UPSIDE: continuing into Spring 2027 may include community-based qualitative analysis, codebook development, coding, and contributing to peer-reviewed papers and policy briefs. Health Justice was founded by Dr. Oni Blackstock.

scoreRationale.qualification: Clears the hard gate outright — CUNY SPH graduate student — and the pool is restricted to CUNY SPH people, which narrows the field sharply. Facilitation experience is the listed soft spot; office hours, trainings, and community intake events are defensible but she needs one specific story for the cover letter.
scoreRationale.enjoyment: Participant-facing, which normally scores down, but it is co-facilitated from a prepared guide alongside a project team member, and the hours-to-stipend ratio makes it worth it on her own assessment.
scoreRationale.school: Confirmed against the Fall 2026 syllabi: classes are Tuesday and Thursday 4-5:50pm, so Wednesday afternoon and early evening sessions are clear. Easiest schedule fit anywhere in the pipeline.
scoreRationale.location: Sessions are at the CUNY SPH building in Harlem where she already attends class, so there is no additional commute.
scoreRationale.mph: Health equity, community governance, and AI in health is current, publishable subject matter directly inside her degree.
scoreRationale.mission: Community-centered health equity research in Harlem, led by a physician-founder, is a strong mission match.

1700000074000.requirements:
Policy research for an industry association of pediatric therapy companies, clinicians, parents, and researchers. Projects may include federal and state policy affecting access to pediatric therapy; Medicaid, commercial insurance, reimbursement and coverage policy; workforce shortages and licensing barriers; access, wait time, and disparity comparisons across states; early intervention and school-based therapy; legislative and regulatory analysis; policy briefs, issue summaries, and educational materials; presenting findings to leadership.

Who should apply: undergraduate and graduate students from all academic backgrounds, including public health, public policy, health policy, healthcare administration, political science, economics, social work, sociology, psychology or child development, education, law, speech-language pathology, and occupational or physical therapy. 1700000074000.notes: Found on Handshake (CUNY SPH board) 8/27/26. BLOCKER — VERIFY EMPLOYER BEFORE APPLYING: the Handshake employer is listed as 'Oaklin Lane' while the posting describes 'The Pediatric Collective,' and that mismatch is unresolved. Confirm the organization is real and that the two names are connected before sending materials. Note also that an industry association advocates on behalf of its member companies, so this is trade-association policy work rather than public-interest policy. Fully remote at roughly 25 hrs/week.

scoreRationale.enjoyment: Owned research projects and brief-writing with no caseload matches her preferences well.
scoreRationale.school: Remote and part-time so class nights are unaffected, though 25 hours a week is a real load.
scoreRationale.location: Fully remote, which removes the commute question entirely.
scoreRationale.mph: Medicaid, coverage, access disparities, and early intervention policy is solid health policy analysis experience.
